sss.quote: Integrity: Hourly accounting, market boundaries reflecting power grid realities, and an incrementality standard (SSS or similar) are critical to ensuring Scope 2 accounting moves forward with transparency and credibility.

Integrity: Hourly accounting, deliverable market boundaries, and an incrementality standard (such as Standard Supply Service or a similar mechanism) are essential to ensuring Scope 2 accounting is transparent and credible.
It would also limit resource shuffling from those same resources, since voluntary claims beyond SSS allocations would need to come from other resources, encouraging purchases from incremental assets.

From an impact point of view this is helpful, as companies that want to make a credible claim of decarbonising their power, would need to invest in storage or additional clean generation that they otherwise would be able to claim if the Standard Supply Service did not exist.

Moving to hourly alignment, using market boundaries that reflect real grids, and applying a clear approach to incrementality (such as SSS or an equivalent) are all necessary steps to strengthen transparency and trust in reported outcomes.

The standard supply service could serve to ensure that only new or additional renewable energy is counted towards emissions reductions, but the definitions of this programmatic backstop still require improvement.

We are particularly motivated to ensure updates are secured around temporal matching and deliverability, as well as guardrails around SSS and further consideration of layered additionality requirements as procurement expands over time.

stronger.quote: Due to these concerns, we think it is critical to have an alternative incrementality pillar definition to be in force before the SSS can be fully implemented or as a backstop in the case of broader implementation challenges.
For greater impact, a stronger incrementality requirement should be developed in place of Standard Supply Service that would drive even greater additionality.
While the SSS can be seen as the incrementality element in this new scope 2 methodology, it presents challenges, such as implementation complexity.
it is critical to have an alternative incrementality pillar definition before the SSS can be fully implemented
The pathway that uses hourly matching and deliverable market boundaries must have a third pillar that addresses incrementality which, if intended, is not addressed by Standard Supply Service (SSS).

Integrity: Hourly accounting, market boundaries reflecting power grid realities, and an incrementality standard (SSS or even better: an asset age limit) will very much increase the integrity of scope 2 reporting.
The asset age limit requirement could be implemented in place of or in conjunction with SSS as it is currently proposed.
First, despite some claims, SSS is not a proxy for additionality, and SSS alone does not ensure that reporting entities prioritize new clean energy development.
